items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: there was a Portugese drummer from Lisbon by the name of BeeBee Miranda

ctx.x: Yes, George, Ginley, one of the wealthiest men in the world and sort of a playboy who loved jazz and we were friends, opened a room called the [Manorchi] (phonetic) which in Portugese means midnight room and they wanted a trio, an American trio and he -- it was a very sort of posh place and he wanted just special musicians and would I get a trio and so I brought Joe Bushkin down, we were talking about that the other night, Joe Bushkin came in this club to see me and a bass player by the name of Herb Warren.

We got down there and realized that we needed a drum and there was a Portugese drummer from Lisbon by the name of BeeBee Miranda, he didn't sticks, he just played with his hands and had little metal things he put on his fingers and he was just a fantastic artist. So we had a fine quartet, bass player --
